memories.memory_text: I told Finley Hollis, 'Listen to me, Finley Hollis; you haven't the strength or the equilibrium,' because I knew he wasn't ready to move yet.

grounded_facts: Elliot York expresses inability to remain passive and asks Graham Mercer for tasks she can perform.
Elliot York asks Graham Mercer how she can help, showing willingness to contribute.
memories.memory_text: I was told Elliot York couldn't just sit there and asked me what she could do to help.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer directs Elliot York to help prepare the surgery area for incoming patients.
Graham Mercer states he expects incoming patients and directs Elliot York to help prepare surgery.
memories.memory_text: I told Elliot York to help get my surgery squared away because I'm expecting incoming patients.

grounded_facts: A combat-induced medical emergency unfolds in the hospital bay as the ship takes damage.
memories.memory_text: I was in the hospital bay when the ship reverberated from a near miss, then another shot hit while I heard someone say they couldn't just sit there—I knew we were in the middle of a combat medical emergency.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott counters Graham Mercer' warning by emphasizing his non-human physiology as justification for entering the radiation zone.
memories.memory_text: Taylor Prescott told me, 'I'm not human,' when I warned him about the radiation, as if that made it okay to walk into a death trap.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer attempts to stop Taylor Prescott from entering the radiation room, questioning his judgment and emphasizing the danger.
memories.memory_text: I tried to stop Taylor Prescott from going into that radiation room because I knew no human could survive it, and I wasn't about to let him throw his life away.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott uses the Vulcan nerve pinch on Graham Mercer to prevent further interference with his entry into the radiation room.
memories.memory_text: I remember Taylor Prescott using the Vulcan nerve pinch on me—I didn't see it coming—and then I was on the floor, helpless.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott decides to enter the highly radioactive reactor room despite warnings, using the Vulcan nerve pinch to incapacitate Graham Mercer when intercepted.
memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Prescott decide to enter the reactor room despite the danger, intercepted him to stop him, heard him say he wasn't human, and then he used the nerve pinch on me—I went down, and through the glass, I watched him walk into that irradiated chamber.

grounded_facts: From a distance, Logan Davenport expresses horror and urges Taylor Prescott to leave the reactor room immediately.
memories.memory_text: I saw Logan Davenport shout in horror, yelling for Taylor Prescott to get out of the reactor room right away.

grounded_facts: Logan Davenport shouts at Evan Grayson through the glass, begging him to intervene and stop Taylor Prescott from sacrificing himself.
memories.memory_text: I saw Logan Davenport yelling through the glass, pleading with the Evan Grayson to stop Taylor Prescott from sacrificing himself.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer shouts at Evan Grayson, urging him to get Taylor Prescott out of the reactor chamber, expressing horror at the situation.
memories.memory_text: I shouted at Evan Grayson, begging him to get Taylor Prescott out of the reactor chamber—oh God, we couldn't just let him die like that.

grounded_facts: The the glass notebook planet is seen evolving on screen, marking a historic moment.
memories.memory_text: I saw the the glass notebook planet evolving on the screen, and it felt like witnessing a moment in history.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer contacts Evan Grayson via intercom with an urgent tone, prompting immediate action.
memories.memory_text: I contacted Evan Grayson over the intercom with an urgent tone because I needed him to come right away.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson departs the Harborview Theater urgently after receiving a distress call from Graham Mercer.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Evan Grayson left the Harborview Theater urgently after I called him, though I didn't see him leave.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson tries to activate the control panel to save Taylor Prescott, but Logan Davenport stops him to prevent disaster.
memories.memory_text: I saw Evan Grayson try to activate the control panel to help Taylor Prescott, so I grabbed him to stop him, and I heard Logan Davenport shout that it would flood the compartment.

grounded_facts: A critical situation requiring manual repair of Harborview Theater's reactor, resulting in Taylor Prescott's fatal radiation exposure.
memories.memory_text: I saw the reactor room's warning light and realized Taylor Prescott had been exposed to fatal radiation while repairing it. I knew there was no way to save him.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott comforts Evan Grayson in his final moments, affirming their friendship and the logic of his sacrifice.
Taylor Prescott delivers a personal and philosophical farewell, referencing the Kobayashi Maru and their friendship.
memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Prescott comfort Evan Grayson in his final moments, telling him not to grieve because the good of the many outweighs the few, and reminding him of their bond by saying he’s always been and always will be his friend — even referencing the Kobayashi Maru test as he faced death.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott dies from radiation exposure after saving the ship by entering the reactor room.
memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Prescott fall after he was exposed to lethal radiation in the reactor room, and I knew he had died saving the ship.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson realizes Taylor Prescott has died after seeing his condition and hearing confirmation from Graham Mercer.
memories.memory_text: I told Evan Grayson that Taylor Prescott was already dead, and I saw him break down when he saw Taylor Prescott's body through the glass.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson mirrors Taylor Prescott's hand on the glass in a final gesture of connection.
memories.memory_text: I watched Evan Grayson mirror Taylor Prescott's hand on the glass, pressing his own hand against it in a silent gesture of connection while I stood by, helpless, seeing the pain tear through him.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson introduces Noel Vale to Casey Rivers with visible hesitation, revealing a personal relationship.
memories.memory_text: I saw Evan Grayson hesitate before introducing the young man as his son — that moment spoke volumes about how personal this was for him.

grounded_facts: Casey Rivers calls Noel Vale 'the dumb bastard' in a dry, ironic tone, then clarifies it as a joke.
memories.memory_text: I heard Casey Rivers call Noel Vale 'the dumb bastard' in that dry tone of hers, and then clarify it was a joke — it almost made me laugh, coming from her.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer suggests the planet might be named after Elliot York; she counters it should honor their friend (implied: Taylor Prescott).
memories.memory_text: I suggested the planet might be named after Elliot York, but she said no—if she could help it, we'd name it for our friend instead.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson declares a renewed sense of vitality, signaling a psychological or emotional transformation.
memories.memory_text: I heard Evan Grayson say, 'Young. I feel young, Doctor,' and I could tell he meant it—he truly felt renewed.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson enters the Harborview Theater accompanied by Noel Vale, introducing a significant familial revelation and initiating new interactions.
The crew is on duty aboard Harborview Theater Harborview Theater while en route to Ceti Alpha, engaging in command交接 and personal exchanges.
memories.memory_text: I was on the Harborview Theater with Elliot York when Evan Grayson walked in with a young man, and I could feel the shift in the air as the crew carried on around us.

grounded_facts: the brass letter is hit multiple times by Klingon photon torpedoes, losing main and auxiliary power, weapons, and life support systems.

memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Prescott waiting for me, and he gave me a book as a gift, which I thanked him for—I even lifted it to show I appreciated it—especially since he mentioned knowing my fondness for antiques.

grounded_facts: An uncelebrated but acknowledged personal milestone for Evan Grayson, referenced by Taylor Prescott.
Taylor Prescott explicitly acknowledges Evan Grayson's birthday by referencing it as 'the best of times'.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Taylor Prescott that it was my birthday, and though I hadn’t brought it up, he acknowledged it as 'the best of times' and wished me a happy birthday.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott observes that something is troubling Evan Grayson, based on his demeanor.
memories.memory_text: Taylor Prescott could tell something was bothering me just by how I was carrying myself, even before I said a word.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott observes and directly questions Evan Grayson's troubled demeanor.
memories.memory_text: Taylor Prescott noticed I was troubled and said, 'Something oppresses you,' and I confirmed it by simply saying 'Something.'

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson enters a turbo elevator and leaves the scene, ending the encounter with Taylor Prescott.
memories.memory_text: I stepped into a turbo elevator and left the scene while Taylor Prescott watched me go.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer presents Evan Grayson with a bottle of illegal Romulan Ale as a birthday gift, using humor and medical justification.
memories.memory_text: I remember Graham Mercer arriving at my apartment with a bottle of blue liquid he called Romulan Ale, joking about 'Romulans bearing gifts' before pouring us both a drink and telling me to open the other present.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer visits Evan Grayson on his birthday and gives him two gifts: a bottle of Romulan Ale and a pair of antique 'Ben Franklin' half-glasses.
memories.memory_text: I remember Graham Mercer coming into my quarters on my birthday with two gifts—one was a bottle of Romulan Ale, which he dramatically revealed, and the other was a pair of antique 'Ben Franklin' half-glasses that I opened after he urged me to, and I could see clearly through them when I looked down.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer teaches Evan Grayson how to properly wear and use the antique half-glasses.
memories.memory_text: I remember Graham Mercer showing me how to wear the antique half-glasses—he told me to slide them down my nose and look over the top, reading through the bottom, and mentioned they were for my eyes since I can't take Retlax Five.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson learns how to use the antique half-glasses, which restore his ability to read without strain, symbolizing a small reclaiming of personal capability.
memories.memory_text: I learned how to use the half-glasses, and when I finally saw clearly, I felt amazed and said to Graham Mercer, 'Amazing! I don't know what to say—' because I could read without strain for the first time in a while.

grounded_facts: A private birthday visit by Graham Mercer to Evan Grayson's apartment, involving gift-giving, drinking, and emotional confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I was with Graham Mercer in my apartment for my birthday, drinking Romulan Ale and opening his gifts, when he challenged me about avoiding command and hiding behind regulations, saying we shouldn't treat my birthday like a funeral.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer directly tells Evan Grayson that he is hiding from himself by staying in a safe administrative role.
memories.memory_text: I was told directly by Graham Mercer that I'm hiding from myself, Evan Grayson—that's what he said to my face.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer challenges Evan Grayson's passive acceptance of desk duty and emotional isolation, urging him to reclaim his command before it's too late.
memories.memory_text: I remember Graham Mercer confronting me, asking why I'm stuck behind a desk when I want to be out exploring galaxies, calling me out for hiding behind rules and regulations—and then driving it home by saying I'm hiding from myself, Evan Grayson.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson and his party are on final approach to the the brass letter aboard a Riverside School shuttle, initiating docking procedures.
memories.memory_text: I was on the shuttle with my party, and I announced our final approach to Harborview Theater as we began docking procedures.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson thanks Sasha Mercer for serving under him, expressing personal appreciation for his presence on the shuttle.
memories.memory_text: I thanked Sasha Mercer personally for serving under me and for being with me on the shuttle—I truly appreciated having him there.

memories.memory_text: I told Sasha Mercer that I had personally cut his new orders, assigning him to command the USS EXCELSIOR by the end of the month.

memories.memory_text: I told Sasha Mercer he's earned his command and that I have full confidence in him, though I joked that I'm not sure these younger officers can steer without him for the next three weeks.

memories.memory_text: I made a dry comment to Casey Rivers about our shared experience with death and life, but she didn't respond well to it.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott exchanges a glance with Evan Grayson before and after assigning Casey Rivers the piloting task, conveying amusement and mutual recognition of the moment's significance.
memories.memory_text: I shared a glance with Taylor Prescott before and after he gave Casey Rivers the order, and in that moment, we both felt the same quiet amusement and understanding about how significant this was.

grounded_facts: Casey Rivers is given the order to pilot Harborview Theater out of Harborview Theater for the first time, marking a moment of responsibility and inexperience.
memories.memory_text: I watched Casey Rivers prepare to take control, knowing this was her first time piloting Harborview Theater out of Harborview Theater, and I felt like a father seeing his child drive the family car for the first time.

memories.memory_text: I tried to reach Elliot York, but the message kept breaking up, and I could barely hear her—I knew something was interfering with our communication.

memories.memory_text: I ordered Sage Delaney to alert Harbor Point Department immediately after the transmission was jammed.

memories.memory_text: I announced to the Harborview Theater crew that I was assuming command of Harborview Theater by Harbor Point Department order due to an emergency, and I instructed the duty officer to log the change and plot a course to Fairview Street.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson declares an emergency and assumes command of Harborview Theater by order of Harbor Point Department.
memories.memory_text: I declared an emergency and assumed command of Harborview Theater by order of Harbor Point Department, making it official at 1800 hours.

memories.memory_text: I ordered Harborview Theater to change course to Fairview Street, and I confirmed that the new course was plotted.

memories.memory_text: I directly ordered Sasha Mercer to engage warp speed at Warp 5.

memories.memory_text: I witnessed Harborview Theater engaging warp engines and going to Warp 5 under my command.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson informs Taylor Prescott of a potential crisis at Fairview Street and the order to investigate, initiating the mission.
memories.memory_text: I informed Taylor Prescott that something might be wrong at Fairview Street and that we'd been ordered to investigate, initiating the mission.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson asks Taylor Prescott about the readiness of the Owen Sawyer under real pressure.
memories.memory_text: I asked Taylor Prescott how well my Owen Sawyer would hold up under real pressure, since we're the only ship in the quadrant and I had told Harbor Point Department they were just children.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott asserts that as the senior officer, he must take command for the actual duty mission, overriding Evan Grayson's initial assumption of leadership.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Taylor Prescott that as the senior officer, he must take command for actual duty, overriding my assumption of leadership based on protocol.

grounded_facts: A conversation between Evan Grayson and Taylor Prescott regarding the mission to Fairview Street, involving command decisions and crew readiness.
memories.memory_text: I discussed the mission to Fairview Street with Taylor Prescott, where I told him to take me there directly, but he reminded me that as the senior officer aboard, I should assume command during actual duty, challenging my initial approach.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott reaffirms his personal and professional loyalty to Evan Grayson, acknowledging both rank and friendship.
memories.memory_text: I remember Taylor Prescott reaffirming his loyalty to me, not just as his superior officer but as a friend, when he said, 'You are my superior officer. You are also my friend. I have been and always shall be yours.'

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson asks Taylor Prescott to join him on the Harborview Theater, signaling reliance on his presence.
memories.memory_text: I asked Taylor Prescott to accompany me to the Harborview Theater because I needed him with me where I could rely on his presence during the mission.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott agrees to join Evan Grayson on the Harborview Theater after coordinating with Logan Davenport, signaling full operational engagement.
memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Prescott agree to join me on the Harborview Theater after he spoke with Logan Davenport to prepare the Owen Sawyer, which told me he was fully committing to operational duty.

grounded_facts: Harborview Theater fails to establish contact with Fairview Street, despite the absence of signal jamming.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Sage Delaney's attempt to contact Fairview Street and saw that we got no response, despite no jamming blocking our signal.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott reports that Fairview Street is not jamming but is not responding, presenting two logical possibilities.
memories.memory_text: I heard Taylor Prescott report that Fairview Street isn't jamming us but isn't responding, and he told me there are two possibilities: they don't want to answer or they can't.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson quotes a prior message: 'Give up the glass notebook,' and questions its meaning and intended recipient.
memories.memory_text: I recalled the message 'Give up the glass notebook' and asked myself what it could mean and who it was meant for, trying to make sense of it.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson decides to bring Graham Mercer into the discussion and moves the conversation to his quarters.
memories.memory_text: I decided to bring Graham Mercer into the discussion and moved the conversation to my quarters, telling Casey Rivers to take command.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson uses his Class 1 security clearance to request and obtain access to the the glass notebook summary from the computer.

grounded_facts: After viewing the the glass notebook tape, Taylor Prescott and Graham Mercer debate the scientific and ethical consequences of the technology.
memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Prescott and Graham Mercer react with shock after we viewed the the glass notebook tape, and I could tell they were about to clash over what it meant.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott clarifies that if the glass notebook is used on a planet with existing life, it would destroy that life to create a new biosphere.
memories.memory_text: I heard Taylor Prescott explain that the glass notebook would destroy existing life on a planet to create a new biosphere, and he insisted it was logical to pursue the knowledge despite the risks.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer accuses Taylor Prescott of being inhuman for dismissing the moral implications of the glass notebook.
memories.memory_text: I remember Graham Mercer lashing out at Taylor Prescott, accusing him of being inhuman for ignoring the moral consequences of the glass notebook, calling it universal Armageddon.

memories.memory_text: I inferred that Elliot Carver was reflecting on his intent for revenge against me, drawing on the idea that revenge is best served cold, framing our conflict as a personal vendetta, though I wasn't certain he truly believed the proverb applied to us.

memories.memory_text: I secretly ordered Casey Rivers to retrieve the small photograph's command console data so we could use the prefix code, telling her to hurry because it was our only chance.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson pretends to search for the glass notebook data to buy time while secretly preparing a countermeasure.
memories.memory_text: I pretended to search for the the glass notebook data to buy us more time, telling Elliot Carver we needed it while knowing he didn't have it yet, and I kept asking for more time because I knew we were running out of it.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott informs the Harborview Theater crew about the prefix code system used to authenticate commands between starships.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Taylor Prescott that the prefix code is 16309, and that each starship has its own code to authenticate commands sent electronically from the Harborview Theater.

grounded_facts: A coordinated effort on Harborview Theater Harborview Theater to send a forged command to the small photograph, aiming to lower its shields during a confrontation with Elliot Carver.
memories.memory_text: I led a coordinated effort from Harborview Theater Harborview Theater to send a forged command using the prefix code, aiming to lower the small photograph's shields during our confrontation with Elliot Carver.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson challenges Elliot Carver on whether he will honor any agreement, seeking assurance before proceeding.
memories.memory_text: I challenged Elliot Carver directly, asking how I could trust him to keep his word before moving forward.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson quietly instructs Sasha Mercer to lock the leather case on target and await further command.
memories.memory_text: I quietly instructed Sasha Mercer to lock the leather case on target and await my command.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson gives the final order to Taylor Prescott to transmit the command after confirming with Elliot Carver that no promise of mercy was given.
memories.memory_text: I gave the order to Taylor Prescott to initiate the shield override after confirming Elliot Carver wouldn't show mercy.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott enters the prefix code 16309 and additional signals into Harborview Theater's weapons console to send a command to lower the small photograph's shields.
memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Prescott enter the prefix code 16309 and other signals into the console to send the command that would lower the small photograph's shields.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson gives a direct order to fire, directing the crew's action.
memories.memory_text: I gave the order to fire, directing the crew to initiate weapons fire immediately.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson angrily dismisses Sasha Mercer's praise, blaming himself for being unprepared and calling himself senile, showing a moment of self-doubt.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Evan Grayson angrily dismisses Sasha Mercer's praise, blaming himself for being unprepared and calling himself senile, showing a moment of self-doubt.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson angrily rejects Sasha Mercer's compliment, expressing frustration and self-criticism.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Evan Grayson angrily rejects Sasha Mercer's compliment, expressing frustration and self-criticism.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson tells Casey Rivers to cease rigid adherence to protocol and focus on assessing the current crisis.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Evan Grayson tells Casey Rivers to cease rigid adherence to protocol and focus on assessing the current crisis.

grounded_facts: Logan Davenport enters Harborview Theater Harborview Theater carrying the dead body of Adrian Marlowe, visibly injured and emotional, signaling a severe crisis aboard the ship.
memories.memory_text: I saw Logan Davenport come through the turbo doors, holding Adrian Marlowe's body, both of them covered in blood, and he collapsed into my arms while I took in the horror of what had happened.

grounded_facts: A post-attack medical emergency in sick bay with multiple casualties and urgent triage.
memories.memory_text: I entered sick bay and saw the chaos of multiple casualties, moving through them to reach Adrian Marlowe while Graham Mercer worked on him and Logan Davenport stood by, visibly shaken.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson reassures dying Adrian Marlowe that the order for warp speed was executed.
memories.memory_text: I told Adrian Marlowe, as he lay dying, that the word was given: warp speed, so he could die knowing his duty was fulfilled.

grounded_facts: Adrian Marlowe succumbs to his injuries after confirming the order for warp speed was given.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Adrian Marlowe asked if the order had been given, and after I confirmed it, he almost smiled and then died peacefully.

grounded_facts: Logan Davenport confronts Evan Grayson with a silent look and a single word — 'WHY' — expressing grief and implied blame over Adrian Marlowe's death.
memories.memory_text: I saw the pain in Logan Davenport's eyes when he looked at me and simply said 'WHY,' holding me responsible for Adrian Marlowe's death.

grounded_facts: The Harborview Theater reports that auxiliary power has been restored, enabling impulse propulsion.
memories.memory_text: I was told the Harborview Theater had restored auxiliary power, so we could proceed at impulse power.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson asks Logan Davenport if main power can be restored, seeking options for mission recovery.
memories.memory_text: I asked Logan Davenport if there was any chance of getting the main power back online, because I needed to know our options for recovering the mission.

grounded_facts: Logan Davenport thanks Graham Mercer for trying to save Adrian Marlowe, showing respect despite loss.
memories.memory_text: I saw Logan Davenport thank Graham Mercer for trying to save Adrian Marlowe, and he squeezed his shoulder before limping away.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson admits to Graham Mercer that he lost the confrontation with the enemy, surviving only due to superior knowledge of the ship.
memories.memory_text: I admitted to Graham Mercer that I got beat, and the only reason we're alive is because I knew something about these ships that the enemy didn't.

grounded_facts: Harborview Theater is nearing the Fairview Street Fairview Street, specifically Fairview Street, indicating a critical phase in the mission.
memories.memory_text: I remember that we were approaching Fairview Street, and the mission was entering a critical phase as we neared the Fairview Street.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson directs Sage Delaney to attempt communication with Fairview Street again.
memories.memory_text: I directed Sage Delaney to try again to establish communication with Fairview Street from Harborview Theater.

grounded_facts: Sage Delaney transmits a message from Harborview Theater to Fairview Street, seeking contact.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sage Delaney transmit a message to Fairview Street, calling out to them to come in, as we sought contact.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson makes the decision to go down to the Fairview Street despite risks and lack of sensor data.
memories.memory_text: I made the decision to go down to the Fairview Street even though we had no sensor data and it was risky.

grounded_facts: Casey Rivers attempts to prevent Evan Grayson from beaming down alone by citing a regulation requiring armed escort for flag officers in hazardous areas.
memories.memory_text: I remember Casey Rivers stepping forward and telling me that General Order 15 required an armed escort for flag officers in hazardous areas, trying to stop me from beaming down alone.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson rejects Casey Rivers's citation of General Order 15, implying it does not exist, undermining her confidence.
memories.memory_text: I told Casey Rivers there was no such regulation when she cited General Order 15, making it clear I wouldn't be deterred from going alone.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson formally transfers command of the ship to Taylor Prescott before departing for the station.
memories.memory_text: I formally transferred command of Harborview Theater to Taylor Prescott, telling him to establish a parking orbit around the station and send me a complete damage report after he contacted Logan Davenport.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott expresses personal concern for Evan Grayson's safety as he departs.
memories.memory_text: As I was leaving, I heard Taylor Prescott tell me to be careful, which stood out because it was one of the few times he openly expressed personal concern for my safety.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson, Casey Rivers, and Graham Mercer materialize in Fairview Street on a Fairview Street, initiating their exploration.
memories.memory_text: I materialized in Fairview Street on the Fairview Street with Casey Rivers and Graham Mercer, ready to begin our exploration.

grounded_facts: Casey Rivers detects ambiguous biological readings using her tricorder, indicating possible unseen presence.
memories.memory_text: Casey Rivers told me she detected indeterminate life signs with her tricorder, so I knew there might be something unseen nearby.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson orders the team to proceed with caution and they begin searching the lab separately.
memories.memory_text: I ordered the team to set the leather case on stun and move out, and we began searching the lab separately.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson expresses stunned disbelief upon recognizing that even the Lane Sterling was killed, emphasizing the brutality of the massacre.
memories.memory_text: I couldn't believe they even killed the Lane Sterling, and I said as much to Graham Mercer—it showed how brutal and senseless this massacre was.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer identifies the dead as known crew members including Riley Wilder, Valerie Colter, the Lane Sterling, and a Elliot North, determining the deaths occurred recently based on body temperature and absence of rigor mortis.
memories.memory_text: I helped Graham Mercer cut down the last of the bodies and recognized Riley Wilder, Valerie Colter, the Lane Sterling, and a Elliot North—crew members I knew—hanging upside down.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer and later Evan Grayson explore a deserted section of the Fairview Street, discovering signs of a recent massacre.
Graham Mercer discovers five bodies hanging upside down in the Fairview Street, which causes initial shock and fear, later leading to examination of the corpses.
memories.memory_text: I helped Graham Mercer cut down the last of the five bodies hanging upside down, and I was stunned when I realized they’d killed the Lane Sterling—this one even looked like a Elliot North.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer reports his medical assessment that the bodies are not warm but lack rigor mortis, indicating the deaths occurred recently.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Graham Mercer that the bodies weren't warm but hadn't stiffened yet, so the deaths must have happened recently.

grounded_facts: After learning the crew was recently murdered, Evan Grayson looks around despairingly and mentions Elliot York, implying fear that she may be in danger or already harmed.
memories.memory_text: I looked around after hearing about the crew's murder and said Elliot York's name, fearing she might be in danger or already hurt.

grounded_facts: Casey Rivers, Evan Grayson, and Graham Mercer discover the unconscious bodies of Finley Hollis and Darian Hollis after hearing a moan and detecting unusual readings on a tricorder.
memories.memory_text: I heard a moan and saw Casey Rivers's tricorder reacting strongly before we opened the door, and then Finley Hollis and Darian Hollis fell out, unconscious.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson tells Casey Rivers to inform Sage Delaney that they are safe in response to her repeated hails.
memories.memory_text: I told Casey Rivers to tell Sage Delaney we're all right because she kept hailing us and needed to know we were safe.

grounded_facts: Finley Hollis wakes up and recognizes Evan Grayson, showing emotional distress.
memories.memory_text: I saw Finley Hollis open his eyes and look right at me, recognizing me in his distress.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson holds Finley Hollis as he weeps upon waking.
memories.memory_text: I held Finley Hollis as he wept like a child after waking up.

grounded_facts: Darian Hollis wakes up and recognizes Graham Mercer.
memories.memory_text: I saw Darian Hollis wake up and recognize Graham Mercer.

grounded_facts: Finley Hollis tells Evan Grayson about Elliot Carver's capture and mind control.
Finley Hollis discloses that Elliot Carver captured them and implanted mind-controlling creatures.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Finley Hollis that Elliot Carver captured them on Ceti Alpha V and implanted creatures in their bodies to control their minds.

grounded_facts: Darian Hollis tells Evan Grayson that the the glass notebook materials and data banks are gone.
Darian Hollis informs Evan Grayson that Elliot Carver could not find the the glass notebook materials, which are gone along with data banks.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Darian Hollis that the the glass notebook materials and data banks were gone, and that Elliot Carver couldn't find them.

grounded_facts: Darian Hollis describes Elliot Carver's torture and murder of scientists, and his narrow escape to attack Evan Grayson.
memories.memory_text: I heard Darian Hollis describe how Elliot Carver tortured and murdered the scientists in a rage when they wouldn't give him information, and how he barely escaped to come after me.

grounded_facts: Darian Hollis reveals that Elliot Carver left the small photograph crew stranded on Ceti Alpha V.
Darian Hollis states that Elliot Carver blames Evan Grayson for his wife's death.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Elliot Carver left the small photograph crew stranded on Ceti Alpha V and that he blames me for his wife's death.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson, having absorbed the information, shifts focus to immediate action by seeking the transporter room.
memories.memory_text: I've absorbed everything I need to know, so I asked where the transporter room is—I'm shifting to action now.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson explains to Casey Rivers that the transporter being left on implies recent use and a sacrifice by the previous crew.
memories.memory_text: I told Casey Rivers that the transporter being left on meant the previous crew had sacrificed their lives to buy escape time for the glass notebook.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson discovers the transporter unit was left on, implying someone used it before the crew's arrival.
memories.memory_text: I noticed the transporter unit was still on, and I realized someone must have used it recently—no one was left alive to turn it off.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott informs Evan Grayson that Harborview Theater has no main power and cannot beam the team back.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Taylor Prescott that Harborview Theater has no main power and won't for at least six days, with auxiliary power possibly restored in two days, meaning they can't beam us back right now.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson establishes a one-hour deadline for contact and orders Taylor Prescott to leave for Star Base if no communication is received.
memories.memory_text: I set a one-hour deadline and ordered Taylor Prescott that if we don't make contact by then, he's to restore what power he can and take Harborview Theater to the nearest Star Base to alert Harbor Point Department.

grounded_facts: Darian Hollis, with Finley Hollis, requests to join Evan Grayson's team despite the danger.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Darian Hollis that he and Finley Hollis wanted to share the risk and join my team for the mission to Fairview Street.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson and team prepare to beam down to the coordinates on Fairview Street, despite uncertainty about the destination.
memories.memory_text: I prepared to beam down to Fairview Street with my team, pointing to the console to confirm the coordinates where they went, and I saw Casey Rivers activate the transport as we vanished together.

grounded_facts: Noel Vale ambushes Evan Grayson, tackling him and holding a knife to his throat, accusing him of causing the deaths of Fairview Street scientists.
Noel Vale confronts Evan Grayson, blaming him for the deaths of the Fairview Street scientists, intensifying hostilities.
memories.memory_text: I was ambushed by Noel Vale, who tackled me and held a knife to my throat while shouting that I was responsible for the deaths of the Fairview Street scientists, saying they could hear the screams all the way to the transporter room.

grounded_facts: Elliot York tells Noel Vale that Evan Grayson is his father, halting the immediate threat of violence.
memories.memory_text: I heard Elliot York tell Noel Vale that he would be murdering his father if he killed me, and in that moment I realized he might be my son.

grounded_facts: Elliot York discloses that Evan Grayson is Noel Vale's biological father, fundamentally altering the emotional and relational dynamics between them.
memories.memory_text: I asked Elliot York if it was true that I was Noel Vale's father, needing to know the truth after everything she had just revealed.

grounded_facts: Darian Hollis confirms his loyalty to Elliot Carver by reporting the situation, establishing Elliot Carver's indirect control over the scene.
Darian Hollis disarms Morgan Mercer and reveals his allegiance to Elliot Carver by reporting to him via communicator, shifting the power balance in the cavern.
memories.memory_text: I saw Darian Hollis disarm Morgan Mercer and speak into his communicator, reporting to Elliot Carver, and then I heard Elliot Carver's voice respond that he had been listening and that Darian Hollis had done well, which made it clear that Elliot Carver was now in control.

grounded_facts: When Noel Vale lunges at Darian Hollis, Darian Hollis reflexively fires his the leather case, killing Morgan Mercer who was behind Noel Vale.
memories.memory_text: I saw Noel Vale lunge at Darian Hollis, and Darian Hollis reflexively fired his the leather case, hitting and killing Morgan Mercer who was standing behind Noel Vale.

grounded_facts: Elliot Carver orders Darian Hollis to assassinate Evan Grayson, exploiting his mental control.
Elliot Carver attempts to command Darian Hollis and Finley Hollis to kill Evan Grayson from a distance via communicator.
memories.memory_text: I heard Elliot Carver's voice over the communicator, commanding Darian Hollis to kill me, and I realized he was trying to control them from a distance.

grounded_facts: Darian Hollis kills himself under Elliot Carver's command after resisting the order to kill Evan Grayson.
memories.memory_text: I saw Darian Hollis turn his the leather case on himself and fire, killing himself after resisting Elliot Carver's order to assassinate me.

grounded_facts: The Ceti eel emerges from Finley Hollis's ear and is destroyed by Evan Grayson.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Ceti eel emerge from Finley Hollis's ear, and as it crawled out, I grabbed a the leather case and destroyed it.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson grabs the wrist recorder used by Elliot Carver to issue commands.
memories.memory_text: After the eel was gone, I saw the wrist recorder Elliot Carver used to command his people and I grabbed it.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson seizes the communicator and directly challenges Elliot Carver after destroying the eel and losing Darian Hollis.
memories.memory_text: With the communicator in hand, I directly challenged Elliot Carver, telling him his plans were finished and he'd have to do his own dirty work now.

grounded_facts: Elliot Carver expresses mock surprise and false camaraderie upon learning Evan Grayson is alive.
memories.memory_text: I heard Elliot Carver express mock surprise and false camaraderie when he realized I was still alive, calling me 'my old friend' with a tone that reeked of deception.

grounded_facts: Elliot Carver successfully beams up the the glass notebook and its arming control box from the cavern, gaining control over the device.
memories.memory_text: I watched helplessly as Elliot Carver beamed up the the glass notebook and its arming control box from the cavern, knowing I had lost control of the device.

grounded_facts: Elliot Carver explains that leaving Evan Grayson marooned is a fitting revenge for how Evan Grayson left him.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Elliot Carver that leaving me marooned was his revenge, that he wished to go on hurting me just as I had left him, and that this was poetic justice.

grounded_facts: Elliot Carver announces his intention to destroy Harborview Theater, rendering it unable to assist Evan Grayson.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Harborview Theater can't move and that Elliot Carver's next act would be to blow her out of the heavens, cutting off any hope of rescue.

grounded_facts: Elliot Carver refuses to kill Evan Grayson directly and instead leaves him trapped on a lifeless planet, declaring it poetic justice.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Elliot Carver refuse to kill me directly, instead trapping me on a lifeless planet and declaring he would leave me buried alive, while also threatening to destroy Harborview Theater so no one could rescue me.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson provokes Elliot Carver to come down to the planet to kill him personally, appealing to Elliot Carver's sense of purpose.
memories.memory_text: I provoked Elliot Carver to come down to the planet to kill me personally, reminding him that he was going to kill me—it was his sole purpose, and he'd have to come down here to do it.

grounded_facts: A final verbal confrontation between Elliot Carver and Evan Grayson via communicator, during which Elliot Carver reveals his revenge and seizes the the glass notebook.
memories.memory_text: I heard Elliot Carver react to my voice, and I spoke to him directly, taunting him as my old enemy — I told him he’d missed his target, but then he declared his intent to hurt me and left me marooned, and I shouted his name in rage as he cut the connection.

grounded_facts: Finley Hollis stirs and moans, attempting to sit up, indicating he is alive and recovering from injury.
Survivors regroup in a rocky cavern after a battle, assessing injuries, communication, and survival options.
memories.memory_text: I saw Finley Hollis stir and moan as we all regrouped in the rocky cavern after the battle, and when someone shouted 'He's alive!', I felt a surge of relief—he was going to make it.

grounded_facts: Casey Rivers reports that all channels are still jammed, making contact with Harborview Theater impossible.
memories.memory_text: I heard Casey Rivers report to me that all channels were still jammed, making it impossible to contact Harborview Theater.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer states that if Harborview Theater obeyed orders, it has left; if it didn't, it is likely destroyed.
memories.memory_text: I heard Graham Mercer say that if Harborview Theater obeyed orders, she's long gone, and if she didn't, she's finished.

grounded_facts: Noel Vale expresses bitterness toward Evan Grayson, blaming him for a man's death due to prior actions.
memories.memory_text: I heard Noel Vale blame me for another man's death, saying it was because of my actions.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer sharply corrects Noel Vale, blaming him for causing two deaths by rushing a man with a primed the leather case.
memories.memory_text: I saw Graham Mercer sharply correct Noel Vale, telling him he caused two deaths by rushing a man with a primed the leather case.

grounded_facts: Elliot York informs the group that there is ample food in the the glass notebook cave, sufficient to last a lifetime.
memories.memory_text: I heard Elliot York say there was food in the the glass notebook cave, enough to last a lifetime, which gave me hope for our survival.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson asks about food, redirecting the group's attention from despair to practical survival.
memories.memory_text: I asked the group if there was anything to eat because I was starved, and I needed to shift our focus from despair to survival.

grounded_facts: Elliot York asks Noel Vale to show Graham Mercer and Casey Rivers the food source in the the glass notebook cave.
memories.memory_text: I heard Elliot York ask Noel Vale to show Graham Mercer and Casey Rivers the food source in the the glass notebook cave.

grounded_facts: Noel Vale is asked by Elliot York and then reluctantly agrees to show Graham Mercer and Casey Rivers the food in the the glass notebook cave.
memories.memory_text: I saw Noel Vale hesitate but then agree to take Graham Mercer and Casey Rivers to the food in the the glass notebook cave after Elliot York asked him.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson responds to Casey Rivers's unspoken concern by quoting Taylor Prescott, affirming belief in possibilities despite dire circumstances.
memories.memory_text: I responded to Casey Rivers's hesitation by quoting Taylor Prescott, telling her that I like to think there are always possibilities.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson shares his deep sense of loss regarding his son and the life he never had with Elliot York.
memories.memory_text: I shared with Elliot York my profound sense of loss over my son and the life I never had with her, opening up about pain I've carried for years.

grounded_facts: A private emotional exchange between Evan Grayson and Elliot York amidst crisis, focusing on their shared past and lost relationship.
memories.memory_text: Elliot York and I had a private, emotional exchange where we confronted the past we lost and the distance between us, with her gently urging me to open up.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson expresses deep emotional pain over the lost relationship with his son Noel Vale and reflects on his aging and weariness.
memories.memory_text: I expressed how deeply I feel the loss of my son Noel Vale and admitted to Elliot York that I'm feeling old and worn out.

grounded_facts: Elliot York responds to Evan Grayson's emotional vulnerability by offering comfort and a chance to reconnect.
memories.memory_text: Seeing my pain, Elliot York responded with compassion, offering comfort and a chance to reconnect by inviting me to experience something that would renew my spirit.

grounded_facts: Elliot York invites Evan Grayson to join her in an unspecified act meant to evoke youth and renewal, leading him toward the tunnel.
memories.memory_text: Elliot York invited me to join her in something that would make me feel young again, and after a moment of hesitation, I took her hand and let her lead me toward the tunnel.

grounded_facts: Elliot York and Evan Grayson move through the tunnel, increasingly excited as they approach a bright, colorful light at its end, with Evan Grayson running ahead.
memories.memory_text: I raced ahead through the tunnel with Elliot York, drawn toward a bright, colorful light at the end that looked blindingly beautiful from my point of view.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson emerges from a tunnel and is awestruck by the vast, Eden-like environment of the the glass notebook Cave, which has been transformed into a lush, habitable ecosystem.
memories.memory_text: I emerged from the tunnel and was awestruck by the vast, Eden-like environment that the the glass notebook Cave had become, lush and teeming with life.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson arrives at the promontory level of the the glass notebook Cave and is met by Elliot York, marking the beginning of his direct engagement with the results of the the glass notebook.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at the promontory level of the cave and was met by Elliot York, marking the moment I began engaging directly with the results of the the glass notebook.

grounded_facts: Elliot York responds to Evan Grayson's amazement by explaining that the matrix formed in a day and life grew rapidly, proudly asking if she can 'Lane Sterling'.
memories.memory_text: I was amazed by the transformation, and Elliot York told me that the matrix formed in a day and life grew rapidly, proudly asking if she could 'Lane Sterling'.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson and others, including Finley Hollis who has been moved to join, eat fruit from the large forest beyond the cave platform.
memories.memory_text: I ate fruit from the forest beyond the cave platform with the others, including Finley Hollis who had just joined us.

grounded_facts: Casey Rivers tells Noel Vale she believes he is the Evan Grayson's son, introducing tension around his identity.
memories.memory_text: I heard Casey Rivers tell Noel Vale she believed he was my son, and I felt the tension rise around his identity.

grounded_facts: Noel Vale and Casey Rivers engage in a tense, wordless exchange of stares after exchanging skeptical remarks about Noel Vale's parentage.
After verbal exchange, Noel Vale returns Casey Rivers's stare, unsettling her, and she challenges him in return.
memories.memory_text: After the exchange about Noel Vale's parentage, I saw him return Casey Rivers's stare in silence, unsettling her, and she challenged him right back.

grounded_facts: A conversation initiated by Casey Rivers about the Kobayashi Maru test, leading to a discussion on facing defeat and Evan Grayson's past actions.
memories.memory_text: I asked Casey Rivers what was on her mind, and she brought up the Kobayashi Maru, wanting to know if we were facing a no-win scenario like the test, and then she asked me directly what I had done during it.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson directly answers Casey Rivers's question about the Kobayashi Maru test by revealing he reprogrammed it, satisfying her curiosity and reinforcing his character.
Evan Grayson discloses that he beat the no-win scenario by reprogramming the simulation, revealing his aversion to losing and demonstrating unconventional problem-solving.
memories.memory_text: I told Casey Rivers I reprogrammed the simulation to make the Kobayashi Maru rescue possible, changed the test conditions, earned a commendation for original thinking, and made it clear I don't like to lose.

grounded_facts: The moment when Evan Grayson contacts Taylor Prescott to coordinate their beam-out from the the glass notebook Cave.
memories.memory_text: I contacted Taylor Prescott to coordinate our beam-out from the the glass notebook Cave, telling him it was time and asking if he was ready, and he confirmed he was on schedule and waiting for my coordinates.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott communicates via voice that he is on schedule and ready to beam Evan Grayson and team aboard, pending coordinates.
Taylor Prescott contacts Evan Grayson via communicator, confirming he is on schedule and ready to beam the team aboard.
memories.memory_text: I heard Taylor Prescott's voice over the communicator confirming he was on schedule and ready to beam my team and me aboard as soon as I sent the coordinates.

grounded_facts: A group arrives on Harborview Theater via transporter, initiating a reunion and immediate tactical discussion.
Evan Grayson, Noel Vale, Casey Rivers, Elliot York, Graham Mercer, and the semi-conscious Finley Hollis materialize in the transporter room.
memories.memory_text: I arrived on Harborview Theater with Noel Vale, Casey Rivers, Elliot York, Graham Mercer, and the semi-conscious Finley Hollis via transporter, reuniting with Taylor Prescott and the others.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson reminds Casey Rivers of Regulation 46-A regarding coded messages during battle, justifying the communication strategy.
memories.memory_text: I reminded Casey Rivers of Regulation 46-A about coded messages during battle to justify our communication strategy.

grounded_facts: Casey Rivers directly accuses Taylor Prescott of lying about the ship's status after recalling regulations.
Casey Rivers accuses Taylor Prescott of lying about the ship's status; Taylor Prescott clarifies he exaggerated, not lied.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Casey Rivers accuse Taylor Prescott of lying about the ship's status, and then heard Taylor Prescott clarify that he had only exaggerated, not lied.

grounded_facts: Graham Mercer announces he is taking Finley Hollis and possibly others to sick bay.
Graham Mercer announces he is taking Finley Hollis to sick bay for medical care.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Graham Mercer announce he was taking Finley Hollis and the others to sick bay for medical care.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott reports that the turbo lift systems are non-functional below C-deck, indicating a critical systems failure in that section of Harborview Theater.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Taylor Prescott that the turbo lift systems are inoperative below C-deck.

grounded_facts: Harborview Theater has achieved partial main power after limited repairs within two hours.
memories.memory_text: I was told we had only partial main power back after two hours of repairs.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson takes command of Harborview Theater Harborview Theater upon arrival, ordering battle stations.
memories.memory_text: I took command the moment I stepped onto the Harborview Theater and ordered battle stations.

grounded_facts: Logan Davenport warns that the energizer is fragile, limiting maneuverability.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Logan Davenport that the energizer is fragile and we shouldn't take too many bumps, which limits how sharply we can maneuver.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson asks Logan Davenport if they can make it into Riverside School, then proceeds despite warnings.
memories.memory_text: I asked Logan Davenport if we could make it into Riverside School, and after he warned me about the energizer, I told him we were going in anyway.

grounded_facts: Evan Grayson decides to pursue the small photograph into Riverside School to gain tactical advantage despite risks.
memories.memory_text: I decided to take Harborview Theater into Riverside School because I knew it could give us a tactical edge, even though we were outgunned and out-run by the small photograph.

grounded_facts: Casey Rivers points out that Riverside School will disable tactical displays and shields.
memories.memory_text: Casey Rivers told me that Riverside School would disable our tactical displays and shields due to the static discharge and gas clouds.

grounded_facts: Taylor Prescott responds to Casey Rivers's warning by reframing Riverside School as an equalizer.
Taylor Prescott notes that Riverside School will negate both ships' advantages, evening the odds.

memories.memory_text: I remember holding the antique book Taylor Prescott gave me, feeling the weight of it, and reading the opening line—'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times'—wondering if there was some deeper message behind it, until he simply said 'happy birthday.'
I admitted 'Something' was troubling me when Taylor Prescott noticed—really noticed—and asked if something oppressed me, and then I stepped into the turbo elevator without saying more.

Graham Mercer walked in with that blue bottle of Romulan Ale, flashed it like a magician, and poured me a drink — I remember squinting at the label, the year '2283,' and feeling the warmth hit me fast, too fast, the moment I tasted it.

He handed me those odd gold half-glasses, made me slide them down my nose and look over the top — I remember the sudden clarity when I saw his face, then the silence that followed, heavy and real, before he told me I was hiding from myself.
I looked up from my book as Sasha Mercer sat beside me and told him I really must thank him — not just for coming back, but for being someone I could still count on in the chair.
I told Sasha Mercer I’d cut his new orders myself — seeing his face when I said he’d have the Excelsior by month’s end, that was something worth remembering.
I boarded Harborview Theater, saluted the Federation symbol, and exchanged salutes with Taylor Prescott. I asked, 'Permission to come aboard, Evan Grayson?'

I saw the wide-eyed young engineer, Adrian Marlowe, snap a stiff salute so earnestly it made me smile — I returned it and asked if it was his first training voyage, then suggested we begin with the Harborview Theater.
I told Taylor Prescott it was his call—'Evan Grayson's discretion'—and saw him smile slightly before giving the order to Sasha Mercer.

I heard Elliot York’s voice breaking through the static, pleading for help—'Please help us, Evan Grayson'—but the transmission kept cutting out, and I couldn’t make out who was taking the glass notebook or on what authority.
After the signal died and Sage Delaney confirmed it was jammed at the source, I slammed the comm panel and ordered her to alert Harbor Point Department—I needed to act before it was too late.
I stepped onto the Harborview Theater and immediately ordered the engines stopped — the crew turned, stunned, as I announced I was assuming command by Harbor Point Department order.
After setting the new course, I called for warp speed and told Sasha Mercer to go to Warp 5 — the ship surged forward as the order took effect.

I remember Taylor Prescott looking up from meditation, so calm, and me telling him we had a problem — that something might be wrong at Fairview Street. He didn't hesitate, just stated the facts like always, but then he said the ship was mine, and I could feel the weight of it, the certainty in his voice even as I tried to brush it off.

He called me his superior, yes, but then he said those words — 'I have been and always shall be yours' — and I nearly couldn't speak. It wasn't just duty; it was personal. When I finally asked him to come with me to the Harborview Theater, it wasn't just for protocol — it was because I needed him there.

I watched the simulation on the screen—dead matter transforming instantly into a living planet, green and swirling with atmosphere. The power of creation... it wasn't just terraforming, it was the glass notebook from nothing.

When the screen showed Fairview Street and Elliot York mentioned the device, I suddenly remembered Finley Hollis was on Riverside Warehouse. I said it out loud—'Finley Hollis's on Riverside Warehouse, isn't he?'—a chill running through me as the threat became personal.
I called yellow alert because Riverside Warehouse's approach didn't make sense—no proper communication, just drifting in, and I could feel the tension building on the Harborview Theater.
I saw his face on the screen—Elliot Carver—and for a moment, I couldn't believe it. The voice, the smile, it was him after all, come back to finish what he started.

I pretended to search for the glass notebook data to buy time, while quietly ordering Casey Rivers to pull up Riverside Warehouse's command console charts and signaling Taylor Prescott to keep nodding like I was giving real orders.
I told Elliot Carver the transmission was coming through, stalling just long enough to keep him from acting before Taylor Prescott could input the code.
I gave the signal—'Here it comes. Now, Taylor Prescott'—softly, watching Taylor Prescott move at the console to enter the prefix code.
I failed us—I let them catch us unprepared, and I can still hear Sasha Mercer’s voice saying I did it, but I didn’t, not really.
Logan Davenport came through those doors carrying Adrian Marlowe, both of them soaked in blood, and the weight of the body nearly pulled me down as he swayed into my arms.
I knelt by Adrian Marlowe as he lay dying, and when he asked if the word was given, I told him yes—warp speed. He almost smiled before he died.

After Adrian Marlowe died, I got on the intercom with Taylor Prescott, heard we had impulse power, and ordered best speed to Fairview Street—then asked Logan Davenport if we could get main power back, knowing we needed every advantage.

I made the call to beam down to Fairview Street, even though we had no sensor data and Elliot Carver might still be down there — if there were survivors, we couldn't leave them, and I wasn't going to send anyone in without me.

I saw Finley Hollis and Darian Hollis collapse out of that compartment, limp and unresponsive — my gut clenched, and all I could say was 'My God!' before I snapped into action, shouting at Casey Rivers to get Sage Delaney and let her know we were still alive.
I held Finley Hollis as he wept, and from him and Darian Hollis I learned Elliot Carver captured them, controlled their minds, failed to find the glass notebook, and killed the scientists in a rage.
After confirming the escape pods were intact, I looked around and asked where the transporter room was — we had to act fast before Elliot Carver could carry out his plan.
I heard Noel Vale shout that the the glass notebook was building to detonation — a pattern Taylor Prescott had never seen — and I barely got out 'How soon' before Noel Vale said we had four minutes.
I shouted into the intercom for Logan Davenport to get me warp speed in three minutes or we'd all be dead, but there was only static — no answer.

I saw Taylor Prescott on his knees inside the reactor room, his hands blackened and face cracked from radiation, struggling to speak through the intercom—he asked if the ship was safe, and when I said yes, he looked satisfied before saying it was logical for him to die because the good of the many outweighs the few.

Taylor Prescott reached his hand toward the glass, and I pressed mine against it from the outside; he told me he had been and always would be my friend, then said 'Live long and prosper' before collapsing—and I screamed 'No!' as he fell, unable to move or respond to Casey Rivers's call about the new world.
I saw the simulation—the dead moon transforming into a living planet, matter reorganizing in seconds. The power of creation... it wasn't just theory, it was real.
When Elliot York mentioned firing the device, I suddenly remembered Finley Hollis was on Riverside Warehouse. That ship was due in that sector—something felt wrong, and I couldn't ignore it.

I told Elliot Carver we were finding the the glass notebook data to buy time, while Casey Rivers pulled up Riverside Warehouse's command console charts—our only real hope was the prefix code, and I knew we had to act fast before he realized we were stalling.

I saw Finley Hollis and Darian Hollis fall out of that compartment, limp and barely alive — my gut clenched when I realized they were alive but compromised, and Sage Delaney's voice kept calling, demanding a response I couldn't give yet.
I told Casey Rivers I reprogrammed the Kobayashi Maru simulation to make winning possible — the look on her face when I said it was worth the risk of getting expelled.
I said 'I don't like to lose' twice — once after explaining the test, and again just before calling Taylor Prescott, feeling the weight of what we were walking into.

relations.relation_summary: Evan Grayson and Elliot Carver share a deeply antagonistic relationship defined by mutual hostility and Elliot Carver's intense desire for revenge. The social relationship evidence consistently highlights Elliot Carver's enmity toward Evan Grayson, rooted in Evan Grayson's past decision to exile Elliot Carver and his crew to a dead planet, which Elliot Carver perceives as a profound betrayal. This act fuels Elliot Carver's vendetta, as he repeatedly references 'poetic justice' and invokes a Klingon proverb about revenge, demonstrating the emotional core of his motivation. Elliot Carver's actions are consistently driven by a need to punish Evan Grayson, culminating in direct threats to maroon Evan Grayson as he was marooned, to kill him, and to destroy Harborview Theater. Evan Grayson, in turn, views Elliot Carver as a dangerous enemy, responding with defiance, sarcasm, and tactical resistance, indicating deep distrust and recognition of the existential threat Elliot Carver poses. Their interactions are marked by confrontational dialogue and psychological warfare, such as when Elliot Carver reacts with electronic shock upon hearing Evan Grayson's voice, underscoring the visceral intensity of their rivalry. Key joint events include Elliot Carver threatening Evan Grayson with a the leather case, demanding the the glass notebook data, revealing his identity and intent to avenge himself, and Evan Grayson's desperate verbal challenges during their final confrontation. These events reinforce their roles as adversaries locked in a life-or-death struggle. The relationship does not evolve toward reconciliation; instead, it escalates in hostility, with Elliot Carver's final actions aimed at Evan Grayson's destruction and Evan Grayson actively leading the defense against him. The dynamic remains fixed in opposition, shaped by past betrayal and Elliot Carver's unrelenting pursuit of vengeance.

Evan Grayson and Graham Mercer share a multifaceted relationship that blends deep personal friendship with a long-standing professional partnership aboard the Harborview Theater. Social relationship evidence consistently highlights their dual roles as both colleagues and close friends, marked by mutual trust, familiarity, and emotional investment. Graham Mercer addresses Evan Grayson by his first name 'Evan Grayson,' enters his private quarters without hesitation, and explicitly declares, 'I'm your doctor and I'm your friend,' underscoring the integration of personal loyalty with professional duty. Their interactions are laced with casual banter, shared rituals like drinking Romulan Ale, and personal gestures such as Graham Mercer giving Evan Grayson a birthday gift, all of which reinforce an intimate, enduring bond. Despite this closeness, their relationship includes moments of conflict, particularly around Evan Grayson's leadership style and avoidance of personal accountability, as seen when Graham Mercer accuses him of hiding behind regulations. These confrontations, however, occur within a framework of care and respect, indicating that their disagreements stem from concern rather than hostility. Joint events further illustrate their interdependence: they repeatedly assume command posts together, respond to emergencies as a team, and engage in critical actions such as restraining Evan Grayson during dangerous moments or discussing duty and age during reflective downtime. Graham Mercer' physical restraint of Evan Grayson and Evan Grayson’s act of changing Graham Mercer’ ear compress demonstrate reciprocal care under pressure. The emotional depth of their bond is most evident in shared moments of grief, where Evan Grayson is visibly affected by Graham Mercer’ tears, suggesting a profound emotional connection. Their relationship evolves not in structure but in depth, with each crisis reinforcing their loyalty. The evidence shows a dynamic of mutual influence—Graham Mercer challenges Evan Grayson’s decisions and urges him to reclaim command, directly impacting Evan Grayson’s choices—while Evan Grayson relies on Graham Mercer for both medical and moral support. This relationship is central to both characters’ emotional and behavioral arcs.

Evan Grayson and Elliot York share a complex, multifaceted relationship rooted in a past romantic involvement, confirmed by multiple references to their history and the fact that they are the parents of Noel Vale. Their emotional connection persists despite time and separation, evident in their charged reunion and moments of vulnerability, such as when Elliot York attempts to comfort Evan Grayson and when they discuss their son and past relationship. The residual intimacy is underscored by Elliot York’s question, 'Were we together?', which reflects both personal reflection and lingering emotional investment. Professionally, they are united through the the glass notebook, where they function as collaborators—Elliot York as the project’s director and Evan Grayson as a key ally in protecting its integrity. Their joint participation in critical events, such as discussing the the glass notebook procedure, observing the rapid formation of the matrix, and running together toward the emerging light, highlights their shared investment in the project’s success and their ability to work in tandem under pressure. These experiences reinforce a dynamic of mutual trust and cooperation. The relationship evolves from a rekindling of past affection into a renewed alliance grounded in both personal and professional stakes, influencing Evan Grayson’s protective stance toward Elliot York and the project, and shaping Elliot York’s willingness to rely on Evan Grayson in moments of crisis. The evidence confirms an enduring bond that blends familial responsibility, romantic history, and scientific partnership.

The relationship between Evan Grayson and Noel Vale is fundamentally defined by their father-son kinship, repeatedly confirmed through explicit dialogue and narrative context. Noel Vale is consistently identified as Evan Grayson's son, both by third parties (Elliot York, Casey Rivers) and by the characters themselves, with multiple instances of Evan Grayson referring to Noel Vale as 'my son' and Noel Vale reciprocating by calling Evan Grayson 'my father' or expressing pride in being his son. Despite this biological and emotional foundation, the relationship is initially marked by intense hostility. Noel Vale physically attacks Evan Grayson, tackling him and threatening him with a knife, while verbally declaring 'I'm going to kill him' and calling Evan Grayson a 'dumb bastard.' This animosity appears rooted in estrangement and unresolved emotional tension, possibly due to Evan Grayson's absence or lifestyle, as suggested by Elliot York's remark about Noel Vale not being 'chasing through the universe with his father.' However, the relationship evolves significantly through shared traumatic and reflective experiences. Both undergo the surreal event of being turned to stone simultaneously, symbolizing a moment of shared vulnerability. More crucially, Noel Vale initiates emotional reconciliation by apologizing to Evan Grayson and affirming his pride in being his son, while Evan Grayson responds with physical affection, hugging Noel Vale in moments of emotional climax. Their dialogue about the importance of facing death and life reflects mutual introspection and a deepening of understanding. These events mark a clear transformation from estranged hostility to a reestablished paternal bond, influencing Evan Grayson's protective behavior and Noel Vale's acceptance of his father's identity and legacy.

The relationship between Evan Grayson and Casey Rivers is primarily defined by a hierarchical yet cooperative dynamic rooted in Harbor Point Department protocol and mission-driven necessity. Evan Grayson consistently assumes the role of commander, issuing direct orders to Casey Rivers during critical operations—such as setting course for Ceti Alpha V, increasing ship power, preparing torpedoes, and retrieving data from Riverside Warehouse—demonstrating trust in her competence under pressure. Casey Rivers, as a trainee and junior officer, follows these directives with precision, reflecting her disciplined, 'by the book' approach. This commander-trainee framework is reinforced through formal interactions like salutes and Harborview Theater protocols, as well as collaborative efforts during simulations and real crises, including the the glass notebook mission and emergency maneuvers aboard Harborview Theater. Evan Grayson actively mentors Casey Rivers, offering advice on retaking the Kobayashi Maru test and acknowledging her developing sense of humor with lighthearted remarks, which she appears to value and reflect upon. Their shared combat experiences—Evan Grayson’s reference to having 'been through death and life together'—suggest a deepening bond forged in high-stakes scenarios, elevating their connection beyond mere duty. Joint events such as approaching the big screen with Taylor Prescott, heading to turbo doors as a team, and exchanging dry, personal comments reveal growing camaraderie and emotional nuance. Notably, Casey Rivers invokes General Order 15 to prevent Evan Grayson from entering a hazardous area, indicating not only professional rigor but also a level of concern that challenges strict hierarchy. The evidence suggests mutual attraction, with dialogue explicitly referencing 'the attraction is mutual' and Evan Grayson making flirtatious observations about Casey Rivers’s demeanor. While the romantic element remains understated and professional boundaries are maintained, it introduces a subtle tension that complements their evolving dynamic. Overall, the relationship progresses from formal command structure to one enriched by trust, shared trauma, mentorship, and hinted personal affection, influencing both characters’ decisions—Evan Grayson’s willingness to delegate critical tasks to Casey Rivers, and Casey Rivers’s integration of Evan Grayson’s guidance into her own development. The evidence is insufficient to confirm whether this attraction is acted upon or how deeply it impacts long-term character arcs, but it clearly adds emotional depth to their professional alliance.

memories.memory_text: I ordered full retreat, knowing we were outmatched—'We're over our heads'—and gave the command to disengage, though it felt like a failure of duty.

I remember the weight of silence after the last hit—the alarms, the smoke, Sage Delaney down, Logan Davenport reporting power loss—and still having to order the leather case fire, though I knew we couldn't win.
Evan Grayson spoke to me, saying we had been through death and life together. I stiffened slightly in response.

After I remarked that Evan Grayson was not what I expected, that he seemed too human, Commander Taylor Prescott corrected me—telling me to control my prejudices and learn tolerance, which he called logical.
I sat in the chair and prepared to take Harborview Theater out of Harborview Theater for the first time. Taylor Prescott said, 'Take her out, Casey Rivers,' and I answered, 'Aye, sir.'
I stopped the turbolift to speak with Evan Grayson, and admitted I felt I had failed the Kobayashi Maru test because I could not resolve the scenario.

I stood there for a moment, caught off guard, as Evan Grayson issued commands without protocol. Then I forced myself to respond — 'Prepare for warp speed' — acknowledging his authority even though I had been in command only moments before.

I remember the moment Evan Grayson turned to me and said, 'Casey Rivers, take the con,' before he and Commander Taylor Prescott left for his quarters. The weight of the command chair felt immediate, though I had no time to process it as the Harborview Theater systems remained tense and silent.
I brought up the visual of Riverside Warehouse on the forward screen when Evan Grayson ordered it, the small vessel appearing as a distant dot growing larger in the void.

I remember Evan Grayson's urgent command cutting through the tension—'Casey Rivers, punch up the data charts of Riverside Warehouse's command console—hurry'—and the weight of my fingers moving over the console, confirming the display: 'On screen...'.

I didn't understand how transmitting a prefix code could lower Riverside Warehouse's shields, not at first — the logic of using our own command system against an enemy ship wasn't immediately clear to me.
I raised my tricorder and saw fluctuating readings—life signs, but indeterminate. The silence of the station made the hum of my equipment feel louder than it should.
I moved to the data bank and began entering access sequences, my fingers moving precisely despite the unease in the air. The system responded slowly, as if resisting interrogation.

I was working at the console when a sound drew my attention; as we approached, my tricorder reacted strongly, and then the door opened to reveal Finley Hollis and Darian Hollis—limp, unconscious, falling out like discarded cargo.
I pointed out that the coordinates were within Fairview Street, a planetoid we know to be lifeless and airless—something didn't add up.
I saw Noel Vale lunge for Darian Hollis and immediately tackled him to the ground — my the leather case drawn, but no time to fire before Darian Hollis shot Morgan Mercer.
I restrained Noel Vale as he tried to rush toward the transporter beam, knowing the attempt would be fatal—only half of him would have materialized if he'd gone.
I kept trying to hail Harborview Theater, but the channels remained jammed—no response, just silence. When I reported it to the Evan Grayson, I knew we were truly isolated.
I looked at Noel Vale and said, 'The Evan Grayson's son,' and for a moment, I almost smiled.
After I almost smiled, Noel Vale just stared back at me, and I felt thrown—so I asked, 'What are you looking at?'
I asked Evan Grayson how he beat the Kobayashi Maru test, and he said he reprogrammed the simulation—changed the conditions so victory was possible.
When I said he never truly faced death in the test, he looked at me and said he faces death every day just by being alive—then repeated, 'I don't like to lose.'
I warned Evan Grayson that entering Riverside School would disable our tactical displays, visuals, and shields due to static discharge and gas clouds.

I sat at the Evan Grayson's chair, the weight of the moment pressing on me as I activated the log. 'Evan Grayson's log. Stardate 8130.3, Harborview Theater on training mission to Gamma Hydra. Section 14, coordinates 22/87/4. Approaching Neutral Zone, all systems functioning.'
I heard the fragmented distress call from the Kobayashi Maru and ordered the intercept course, despite knowing we risked crossing into the Neutral Zone.
I stood on the Harborview Theater after the simulation ended, the wreckage still fresh in my eyes, and asked permission to speak candidly—I had to tell him it wasn't fair.
When I said there was no way to win, my voice caught—it was the first time I truly understood that failure could be inevitable, and that admission felt like a failure in itself.

I was working at the console when a sound caught my attention—something didn't align. As I moved toward it, my tricorder began reacting strongly, and then we opened the door to find Finley Hollis and Darian Hollis collapsed inside.
I was at the console when we found Finley Hollis and Darian Hollis. Evan Grayson told me to tell Sage Delaney we were all right while her voice was still calling in the background.

I asked Evan Grayson what he did on the Kobayashi Maru test, and he said he reprogrammed the simulation so it was possible to win—I couldn't believe a cadet could change the conditions of a Harbor Point Department exam.

When I realized he had never actually faced death in the test, Evan Grayson told me we face death every day we're alive—it was said simply, but it unsettled something in my understanding of duty and command.
I stood among the crew in full dress uniform, my hair down, as Evan Grayson began the burial service under the newborn planet’s glow.
When the Evan Grayson faltered and called my name, I stepped forward and spoke the words: 'We commend the soul of our brother departed.'
